title: CP-SAT assumptions as a conflict finder

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: After an INFEASIBLE solve with assumptions, sufficient_assumptions_for_infeasibility() returns [41, 57]. What are these numbers?

options.text: Indices of the assumed flag variables, to map back to rule names
options.says: Right: the call returns variable indices; keep a map from index to rule name.

options.text: Row numbers of constraints, counted in the order they were added
options.says: The flags are variables, and the numbers are their indices.

options.text: Positions in the list of assumptions you passed, counted from zero
options.says: The indices are the variables' own, not positions in the list.

options.text: Hashes of the rule names, which the solver keeps for itself
options.says: The solver knows no rule names; your program supplies them.

origin.section: Assumptions Need Flags, One Worker and a Map From Index to Name

questions.stem: On a ward roster, CP-SAT names 4 flags as a sufficient set. Before the ward manager is told that these 4 rules are the conflict, what should the program do?

options.text: Nothing, since CP-SAT's 4 flags are minimal by definition
options.says: The set is sufficient, not promised minimal; lesson 4.6.2 saw all 28 flags.

options.text: Solve again with eight workers to shrink the 4 flags
options.says: Assumptions need one worker; more workers do not shrink the set.

options.text: Report all the roster's flags, since the 4 flags can be false
options.says: A sufficient set is infeasible, as claimed; it may only be larger than needed.

options.text: Run a deletion filter on the 4 flags, one solve per flag
options.says: Right: it confirms the set is minimal, or shrinks it, for 4 more solves.

origin.section: Here the Solver Named a Minimal Set at Once, So Every Conflict Costs One Solve

questions.stem: Planners ask for the fewest rules to drop so that a plan exists. Which CP-SAT approach answers that?

options.text: Assume every flag and read the set the solver names
options.says: That names one conflict; dropping rules must end every conflict.

options.text: Leave the flags free and maximize how many stay on
options.says: Right: the switched-off flags then hit every conflict, as few as possible.

options.text: Filter the flags and switch off the conflict it keeps
options.says: A conflict is one clash; switching it all off is rarely the fewest.

options.text: Assume every flag false and read which ones turn on
options.says: Assumed values are fixed; the solver cannot turn them on.

origin.section: The Fewest Rules to Switch Off Is an Optimization, Not an Assumption
